data.claim: Mostly yes at the primitive level: gate pipelines (gates.task_pipeline/kind_pipelines/promotion_pipeline), human gates, review round budget and delta, triage, approvals, enforce hooks, worktree per item, flow.integration=pr, cadence and lessons exist. Missing: a named layered workflow profile binding stages to pipelines, a routing predicate classifying item to path, per-round reviewer escalation, advisory review mode with operator-only disposal, stage-scoped human confirmation with a bounded rework loop, task definition of ready, token-threshold handoff note, PR evidence template and branch-policy check, independent acceptance, retrospective proposals targeting rules/guards/checks. Most are already planned as LF-*, QA-*, CC-*, WD-*, P-observe.retro tasks; the profile glue (LF-profile) exists but has no strict-delivery profile, routing or per-stage review policy.
data.falsifier: A walk of the diagram on a sample project with the strict-delivery profile that crosses a stage with an unrun check, lets an agent dispose a finding under dispose_by=operator, or runs the strongest reviewer on a delta instead of the full final diff, or a user-layer profile that loosens a company floor.
data.mechanism: A workflow profile is a layered record (shipped < company < project < user, user highest per D-config-layer-order and D-user-highest-precedence-2026-11-06, company floors tighten-only per LF-profile) naming stages; each stage has entry conditions (DoR predicate), a gate pipeline, a review policy (round ladder, advisory or blocking, who disposes), a human checkpoint flag, evidence required, an on-refusal return stage with a cap, and handoff and retrospective triggers. Routing predicates reuse the guidance engine over item kind, tags, size and globs. Stage checks are existing gates; checkpoints are existing approvals; retrospective and handoff thresholds ride the SJ-* scheduler and context advisor.
data.probe: ddflow brief; ddflow workflow state; ddflow config (gates, review, approvals, enforce, flow, cadence, lessons, handoff); ddflow task list --match profile|checkpoint|escalat|triage|handoff|acceptance|retrospective; ddflow show LF-profile LF-stage-gates LF-operator-points US-ready TM-tdd P-observe.retro
data.probe_output: gates.kind_pipelines={} by default; task pipeline research..merge; review.max_rounds, delta_default, fix_round_free; flow.integration=merge default, pr_reviewers and pr_merge exist; cadence.lessons_pass_every_phases=4; lessons.require_regression_test=True; no per-round reviewer key; no workflow profile record; LF-profile needs LF-profile-design

data.body: Today reviewers are picked per gate ([[reviewer]].gates) and rounds are only counted ([review].max_rounds, delta_default, --delta). [review].ladder is an ordered list of {tier|reviewer, scope delta|full, family_rule}; the picker honours independence (author never counts, DX-reviewer-independence-picker); the final rung is forced full, even when delta_default is true; gate status prints the rung. Falls back to the next reviewer and records unavailable, never passed. Acceptance: round 3 selects the strong reviewer with a full-diff scope while rounds 1-2 use the cheap one with a delta; test fails before the ladder exists. Estimated size: M (about 260 lines). Falsifier: a profile needs a new gate engine instead of kind_pipelines. EXTENSION CONTRACT 2026-11-03 (D-extension-contract-answers): implement this as a feature manifest (ddflow/features/NAME.toml) plus the matching registry (gate plugin, join policy, optimizer provider, proposal kind, notice, predicate, section) instead of a special case or an edit to a shared hub file (defs.py, inbox.py, policy.py, flowsignals.py, health.py, README, config.py, mcp.py). ORIGINAL TEXT (before RH-contradictions-2026-10-18):
ddflow retro run [--scope project|phase|week] renders an overridable prompt with the findings digest, relevant decisions, lessons and safeguards, and bounded log slices, and sends it to a reviewer endpoint of a DIFFERENT model family than the working agents (reviewers machinery) or files it as a research item for an agent (B-sched-run). The output must be structured: observation, cited finding and event ids, hypothesis, proposed change, expected metric effect, risk, falsifier. A verifier re-derives every cited number and event from the log; an unsupported claim is kept but marked THEORETICAL, never proposed as fact. Output is fenced data. Knobs: model endpoint, token budget per run, slices, cadence. Honest limit: LLM-as-judge bias is why the checker is deterministic.
